text:
A: Hello, er, you alright? Can you hear me?
B: Yeah! Hiya, sorry, I'm Holly. I'm in Stockport.
A: Callum. Taunton. Nice to meet you.
B: You too. Erm, sorry, is that a guitar behind you?
A: Ha, yeah. I play it badly. Folk stuff, bit of old blues. There's a session night in a pub in town, I mostly just sit and listen, to be honest.
B: That's so cool though. I can't play anything. I just make playlists. Like, loads of them. I've got one called "train's late again".
A: That's a good name for a playlist.
B: It gets a lot of use, haha. So what do you do?
A: I'm a joiner. Windows, doors, old houses mostly. Sash windows are my favourite. You take one apart and you can sort of see how some bloke did it by hand a hundred and fifty years ago, every mark. Proper satisfying. We've got a Victorian one on at the minute with the original shutters still in the walls. Sorry, I'm going on.
B: No, that's actually really interesting. I'm an apprentice too, sort of. Lab technician. Quality control, testing samples and that.
A: Oh, nice. I did an apprenticeship, four years. Best thing I did, honestly. Are you enjoying it?
B: Erm, yeah, I am. I like the actual lab bits. I'm just rubbish at the portfolio stuff, I keep leaving it till the night before and then panicking. Is that, like, normal, or is it just me?
A: Mate, I'm thirty and my boss is still chasing me for job sheets. I write cut lists on bits of offcut and then lose the offcut.
B: Haha, no way. That makes me feel so much better.
A: I reckon if you're good at the actual job, that's the hard bit. The paperwork you can learn. That's what I tell myself, anyway.
B: Yeah. I worry about it though. Like, I want to do a degree apprenticeship after, and I'm like, how am I gonna organise that when I can't even remember my lanyard?
A: Ha. You'll be fine. Do you get to do proper experiments, or is it more routine?
B: Mostly routine. Titrations, logging results in Excel. But I like it when it all comes out right, do you know what I mean? It's kind of calming.
A: Yeah, that's like a good joint. Fits first time and you're buzzing all day.
B: Exactly! Sorry, what's that bowl on your shelf? Did you make it?
A: Yeah, turned it in the garage. I've got a little workshop, well, half my stepdad's garage. I'm back at my mum's at the minute.
B: I live with my mum as well, so. No judging.
A: Cheers. Your room looks nicer than mine, mind.
B: It's not, there's a crochet bag I've not touched in months and my dog's asleep on my bed.
A: What kind of dog?
B: Staffy cross, Bonnie. She's old, she just snores. Erm, I think she's...
